# Doorbell camera

> Overview type `doorbell` (since 1.7). Entity: required, a `binary_sensor` or `event` or `button` or `input_button` or `input_boolean` entity. Card type `custom:houseview-doorbell-overview-card` (widget type `doorbell_overview`), screensaver `type: doorbell`.

A full-screen camera stream that appears over the dashboard **by itself** when the doorbell rings, and goes away after
a set time. A tap on it closes it sooner and returns to the view you were on; it stays closed until the doorbell has
rung again. Like the timer display it is an **event** overview. It also works as a page card
(`custom:houseview-doorbell-overview-card`; a tap opens the stream full screen).

It is an extra feature of the card, not a screensaver: set it in the editor's **Doorbell camera** section or with the
`doorbell` option, and it is not offered in the screensaver list.

```yaml
type: custom:houseview-card
cards:
  - type: custom:houseview-clock-card
doorbell:
  entity: binary_sensor.front_doorbell
  camera: camera.front_door
  duration: 30
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| entity | entity | required | The doorbell: a `binary_sensor`, `input_boolean`, `event`, `button` or `input_button` |
| camera | entity | none | The `camera.*` entity to show |
| duration | number | 30 | Seconds the stream stays up (5 to 600) |
| name | text | camera name | Used for the title bar and the screen reader label (YAML only) |

The doorbell **rings** when a `binary_sensor` or `input_boolean` turns `on`, or when an `event`, `button` or
`input_button` was pressed less than `duration` seconds ago (their state is the time of the last press). The camera
stays up for `duration` seconds from that press. A binary sensor that turns off again does not close it: a doorbell
often reports on for about a second (shown as Detected, then Clear) and the press time is remembered.

The picture comes up in two steps, both from your own Home Assistant. A still (`camera_proxy`) is shown as soon as it
decodes, and the MJPEG stream (`camera_proxy_stream`) covers it once a frame has loaded. While the dashboard is open
a still is kept warm and refreshed every few seconds, so a ring can show the last frame before the new request
returns. A stream that fails leaves the still up and is retried every ten seconds.
